candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this mandatory testing obligation applies to a given facility/discharge point determines if WET monitoring was required for FY2025; scope and cross-references elsewhere could change applicability classification.

Interpretation of which outfall(s) fall within '001' bounds which discharge points are in scope for limit comparison (A), monitoring obligation evaluation (B), and missing-evidence cases tied to that outfall (C).
How 'reported as final outfall' maps to monitored discharge points affects which measurements and requirements are evaluated under A/B/C for a selected facility.

The 23% critical dilution is the operative compliance threshold referenced by the acute test failure definition; a different reading of this value or its role changes whether reported WET results exceed the applicable limit.

Required dilution concentrations govern how tests must be run and how NOEC/failure are determined; different interpretation of the prescribed series affects compliance comparison (A), whether testing met permit conditions (B), and whether results are adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sample-type requirements are incorporated only by reference to PART I; unresolved or alternate readings of that cross-reference change what sampling/monitoring was required (B), what limit/measurement pairing is valid (A), and how missing or NODI results should be classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur. Acute test failure is defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: These definitions set the enforceable compliance standard for WET (pass/fail relative to critical dilution and statistical significance); different interpretations of NOEC, failure, or the 95% confidence criterion change whether a reported measurement exceeds the applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether an incomplete or terminated test satisfies this completion requirement affects monitoring-obligation compliance (B) and whether the absence of a final result is documented non-requirement, inadequate evidence, or an unresolved case (C).

candidates.locator: page 13, part_i, section D introductory paragraph
candidates.exact_span: It is unlawful and a violation of this permit for a permittee or his designated agent, to manipulate test samples in any manner, to delay sample shipment, or to terminate or to cause to terminate a toxicity test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether sample manipulation, delayed shipment, or test termination occurred affects how missing or irregular WET evidence is classified rather than treated as ordinary no-data.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether QA/method failures trigger a mandatory retest changes if monitoring was still required after an initial run (B), whether a non-repeat result can be used for limit comparison (A), and whether a missing result reflects invalid testing versus acceptable no-discharge or not-required states (C).
